dedupe_keys.name: inventory of past mine production footprints in alaska including land disturbance and potential above ground resources usgs 2024

description: Two polygon shapefiles that outline the footprints of land disturbance and of waste that may be potential above-ground resources left by past mining in Alaska. The ScienceBase page says the footprints were mapped on 2023 World Imagery (imagery dated 2018 to 2023) at currently inactive Alaska Resource Data File (ARDF) sites of past production. The data release by Adrian M. Bender was published on 17 September 2024 and holds a disturbance footprints shapefile (about 0.9 MB zip), a potential above-ground resources shapefile (about 0.7 MB zip) and FGDC metadata in HTML and XML, free under CC0 1.0 as a US federal product. Coverage is the state of Alaska. Caveats: the mapping is visual interpretation of basemap imagery, only inactive ARDF sites with past production are included, and 'potential resources' are waste areas, not measured reserves. For simulation it gives legacy mine disturbance polygons for exposure studies, such as runoff or slope hazards near roads and rivers, and for screening mine waste as a source of critical minerals. Related catalogue records include USMIN mine features from USGS topographic maps and the Australian Mine Waste Database.
